incident_description: During the construction of a multi-story building, a worker was struck by a falling piece of rebar from an upper floor. The worker sustained a fractured arm and head lacerations, requiring hospitalization.

why_chain.question: Why did the rebar fall and strike the worker?
why_chain.answer: The rebar was unsecured and dislodged from a rebar cage being assembled on the 6th floor, falling through an open shaft.

why_chain.question: Why was the rebar unsecured and dislodged?
why_chain.answer: Workers on the 6th floor were assembling the rebar cage without proper temporary securing methods for individual rebar pieces before the full cage was tied, and the work area was not adequately barricaded below.

why_chain.question: Why were workers assembling the rebar cage without proper securing methods and inadequate barricading?
why_chain.answer: The site-specific work method statement (WMS) for rebar cage assembly did not explicitly detail temporary securing procedures for individual rebar pieces during assembly, nor did it mandate specific barricading requirements for falling object hazards during this task. Furthermore, the supervisor did not enforce existing general falling object prevention rules rigorously.

why_chain.question: Why did the WMS lack these critical details and why was enforcement lax?
why_chain.answer: The WMS was developed by the project's HSE department and construction management without sufficient input from experienced rebar workers or a thorough task-specific risk assessment that identified the specific hazard of individual rebar pieces falling during cage assembly. The project management also prioritized schedule over thorough safety planning and supervision.

why_chain.question: Why was there insufficient input and a lack of thorough risk assessment, and why was schedule prioritized over safety planning?
why_chain.answer: The company's safety management system (SMS) had a weakness in its WMS development process, specifically lacking a mandatory requirement for multi-disciplinary review (including frontline workers and supervisors) and a robust task-specific risk assessment for all high-risk activities. Additionally, there was an organizational culture where production targets were implicitly or explicitly given higher priority than detailed safety planning and adherence, leading to inadequate resource allocation for safety planning and supervision.

root_cause: Organizational culture prioritizing production over safety planning and an inadequate safety management system (SMS) process for WMS development and risk assessment.
contributing_factors: Inadequate site-specific work method statement (WMS) for rebar cage assembly.
Insufficient task-specific risk assessment for rebar work at height.
Lack of rigorous enforcement of general falling object prevention rules by supervision.
Inadequate temporary securing methods for rebar during assembly.
Open shaft below work area without sufficient protective measures.
corrective_actions: Immediately revise the WMS for rebar cage assembly to include explicit temporary securing procedures for individual rebar pieces and mandatory barricading requirements.
Conduct a thorough task-specific risk assessment for all rebar work at height.
Provide immediate refresher training to all rebar workers and supervisors on falling object prevention and WMS adherence.
Implement immediate physical barricades and netting around all open shafts and areas below work at height where falling objects are a risk.
Disciplinary action for the supervisor who failed to enforce existing safety rules.

incident_description: During the construction of a multi-story residential building, a worker was struck on the head by a falling wrench from an upper floor. The worker sustained a minor concussion and required medical attention.

why_chain.question: Why did the worker get struck by a falling wrench?
why_chain.answer: A wrench fell from an upper floor and hit the worker below.

why_chain.question: Why did the wrench fall from the upper floor?
why_chain.answer: A worker on the 6th floor was using the wrench and it slipped from their grasp while they were working near an unguarded edge.

why_chain.question: Why did the wrench slip from their grasp and fall over an unguarded edge?
why_chain.answer: The worker was not using a tool lanyard to secure the wrench, and the edge of the slab where they were working did not have adequate toe boards or netting to prevent falling objects.

why_chain.question: Why were tool lanyards not being used and why were there inadequate edge protection measures?
why_chain.answer: The site's 'Working at Height' procedure did not explicitly mandate the use of tool lanyards for all hand tools when working at height, and the inspection checklist for edge protection did not specifically include requirements for toe board height or object fall prevention netting.

why_chain.question: Why did the 'Working at Height' procedure and inspection checklist have these deficiencies?
why_chain.answer: The existing 'Working at Height' procedure and associated inspection checklists were last reviewed and updated over three years ago and did not incorporate best practices for dropped object prevention, nor did they reflect the specific risks of this particular project. There was no systematic process for regular, comprehensive review and update of HSE procedures based on industry standards or incident trends.

root_cause: Prosedür / sistem eksikliği (Lack of a systematic process for regular, comprehensive review and update of HSE procedures, leading to outdated and inadequate 'Working at Height' procedures and inspection checklists regarding dropped object prevention).
contributing_factors: Lack of immediate supervision to ensure adherence to safe work practices (e.g., tool security).
Insufficient training on dropped object prevention for workers operating at height.
Inadequate hazard identification and risk assessment for falling objects during daily pre-task planning.
corrective_actions: Provide immediate first aid and medical attention to the injured worker.
Secure the area where the incident occurred and conduct a thorough investigation.
Implement immediate temporary measures for dropped object prevention (e.g., exclusion zones, temporary netting) in similar work areas.
Retrain all workers on the 6th floor (and similar work areas) on the importance of tool lanyards and dropped object prevention.
Review and update the 'Working at Height' procedure to explicitly mandate tool lanyards for all hand tools and specify requirements for toe boards and netting for dropped object prevention.

incident_description: A miner, John Doe, tripped and fell on an uneven section of the haulage road while walking to the underground workshop. He sustained a sprained ankle and minor abrasions.

why_chain.question: Why did John Doe trip and fall?
why_chain.answer: He tripped on an uneven section of the haulage road.

why_chain.question: Why was the haulage road uneven?
why_chain.answer: There was a build-up of loose rock and debris, creating an irregular walking surface.

why_chain.question: Why was there a build-up of loose rock and debris?
why_chain.answer: The regular road maintenance schedule, specifically sweeping and grading, had been delayed due to equipment breakdown and a shortage of personnel.

why_chain.question: Why was the road maintenance schedule delayed?
why_chain.answer: The primary road grader was out of service for an extended period awaiting a critical spare part, and the available maintenance crew was understaffed due to recent resignations and a hiring freeze.

why_chain.question: Why was there an extended delay for the spare part and a hiring freeze?
why_chain.answer: The mine's procurement process for critical spare parts was inefficient and lacked contingency planning for long lead times, and the company had implemented a cost-cutting measure that included a hiring freeze across non-production departments, impacting maintenance staffing levels.

root_cause: Inefficient procurement process for critical spare parts and company-wide cost-cutting measures (hiring freeze) impacting maintenance staffing and equipment availability.
contributing_factors: Lack of immediate alternative equipment for road maintenance.
Insufficient supervision of road conditions during maintenance delays.
Miners not being explicitly warned about deteriorating road conditions in that specific area.
corrective_actions: Immediately clear the affected section of the haulage road of all loose rock and debris.
Repair the primary road grader and ensure it is fully operational.
Implement temporary manual sweeping and grading until the grader is back in service.
Communicate the current condition of the haulage road to all personnel using it.

incident_description: During routine inspection, a significant leak of natural gas was discovered from a flange connection on a high-pressure gas pipeline. The leak was detected by a portable gas detector and confirmed visually by bubbling in a soap solution. The area was immediately cordoned off, and emergency procedures were initiated to depressurize the affected section of the pipeline.

why_chain.question: Why did the natural gas leak from the flange connection?
why_chain.answer: The gasket within the flange connection failed, leading to a loss of seal integrity.

why_chain.question: Why did the gasket fail?
why_chain.answer: The gasket material degraded prematurely due to exposure to the gas stream and operating temperatures, exceeding its expected lifespan.

why_chain.question: Why did the gasket material degrade prematurely?
why_chain.answer: The selected gasket material was not suitable for the specific chemical composition and temperature fluctuations of the natural gas being transported.

why_chain.question: Why was an unsuitable gasket material selected?
why_chain.answer: The initial design specifications for the pipeline section did not adequately account for the full range of gas stream properties (e.g., trace contaminants, maximum temperature excursions) that would be experienced during operation.

why_chain.question: Why did the design specifications not adequately account for the full range of gas stream properties?
why_chain.answer: The design process relied on generalized industry standards and historical data from similar, but not identical, gas streams, without conducting a thorough, project-specific material compatibility assessment for the anticipated operating conditions.

root_cause: Design flaw: Inadequate material selection due to insufficient project-specific material compatibility assessment during the design phase.
contributing_factors: Lack of comprehensive material compatibility testing for the specific gas stream during engineering design.
Reliance on generic industry standards without detailed analysis of project-specific operating conditions.
Insufficient review of design specifications by an independent expert with specialized knowledge in material science for gas applications.
corrective_actions: Isolate and depressurize the affected pipeline section.
Replace the failed gasket with a material proven to be compatible with the specific gas stream and operating conditions.
Conduct a thorough inspection of all similar flange connections in the affected pipeline section and replace any gaskets showing signs of degradation or using the same unsuitable material.
Perform a leak test on the repaired section before returning to service.

incident_description: During the installation of a new electrical panel in a construction site office, an electrician received an electric shock when attempting to connect a live circuit. The electrician sustained minor burns to their hand and arm and was taken to the hospital for observation. Work was immediately stopped in the area.

why_chain.question: Why did the electrician receive an electric shock?
why_chain.answer: The electrician touched a live electrical circuit while working on the new panel.

why_chain.question: Why was the circuit live when the electrician was working on it?
why_chain.answer: The circuit breaker for that specific circuit was not locked out/tagged out (LOTO) and was inadvertently re-energized by another worker.

why_chain.question: Why was the circuit breaker not locked out/tagged out (LOTO) properly?
why_chain.answer: The LOTO procedure for isolating individual circuits was not clearly communicated or consistently followed by all personnel on site.

why_chain.question: Why was the LOTO procedure not clearly communicated or consistently followed?
why_chain.answer: There was no recent refresher training on LOTO procedures, and the existing LOTO signage and documentation were outdated and difficult to understand.

why_chain.question: Why was there no recent refresher training and why were LOTO materials outdated?
why_chain.answer: The site's electrical safety maintenance program, which includes regular review and update of procedures and training schedules, had not been implemented or followed for over a year.

root_cause: Inadequate maintenance of the electrical safety program, specifically the lack of regular review and update of LOTO procedures and training schedules.
contributing_factors: Lack of clear and consistent communication regarding LOTO procedures.
Inadvertent re-energization of the circuit by another worker.
Insufficient supervision to ensure adherence to safety protocols.
corrective_actions: Immediately conduct a comprehensive LOTO training session for all electrical personnel on site.
Update all LOTO procedures, signage, and documentation to be clear, concise, and easily accessible.
Implement a strict LOTO verification process before any electrical work commences.
Review and update the site's electrical safety maintenance program to ensure regular audits and training.
